rule: Sustained Red (sustained_red_days of sustained_red_window, or any joint >= 4) hands off to replan for a reactive deload; non-joint triggers are a proposal (v1, safety)
summary: Expert consensus treats deloads as a fatigue-management tool and supports reacting to accumulated fatigue, and overreaching studies show a reduced-load week reverses functional overreaching. No trial tests 'n Red days -> deload'; the HRV-guided trials only shift intensity day by day. A planned 1-week deload in trained lifters cost some strength, so false-positive deloads are not free - the proposal gate (athlete approval for non-joint triggers) is the right brake. Safety rule: kept as is.

sources.note: Delphi of 21-34 expert coaches: deloading is reduced training stress to mitigate fatigue and restore preparedness; reactive use endorsed
Triathletes overreached by 3 weeks overload (-9% performance) supercompensated after a 1-week taper
A 1-week full training break mid-programme reduced lower-body strength gains vs continuous training; hypertrophy unchanged - unnecessary deloads have a cost
HRV-guided endurance training mostly removed individual hard sessions rather than whole weeks; small performance benefit, fewer non-responders
